admission.justification: Two real placements were weighed and rejected for named reasons, and the choice binds how any later serving work is scheduled.

alternatives.option: Keep background work in-process, on its own bounded pool, and stop walking worktrees in the recurring fingerprint
alternatives.reason: It removes the queueing between a read and background work and the recurring walk without a second process to supervise or a change to the projection's contract.

alternatives.option: Move the projection into its own process
alternatives.reason: It would also remove shared-heap churn, but it adds a supervised process, its lifetime and its failure modes to a serving path this leaf cannot measure installed.
alternatives.reconsider_when: An installed profile still shows a read starved by background work after this pool and the walk removal.

alternatives.option: Stop dumping the projection on a heartbeat at all
alternatives.reason: It changes the age-resolution contract readers rely on, which is outside this requirement's preservation boundary.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The projection's age semantics are re-opened by an approved requirement.

consequences: Background units run on a process-wide four-thread pool.
The projection's live fingerprint reads native generations instead of walking worktrees.
The installed before/after measurement remains the Architect's.
context: A review read shared the event loop's default executor with the serving projection, so a long projection unit could hold the thread the read needed, and the projection paid a whole-worktree walk on every heartbeat.
decider: The developer's D337 task and MIK-R179 rule 2; the leaf chose among the options the requirement names.
